reasons: Classification is correct: Article III vests ownership of the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights (which via p0015 sweeps in 'all additions, improvements and accessions' and via the Derivative Work definition any enhancements) in Licensor, and the Licensee's only rights are a non-exclusive, field-of-use-limited licence expiring with the 36-month term. That fails both the preferred position (no assignment of paid-for deliverables) and the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables), so a deviation with a redline is warranted rather than over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

Redline is actionable and correctly directed: it is appended as a 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' carve-out that (i) assigns Licensee ownership of the customization/front-end deliverables it funds under Article VII(b), (ii) preserves Licensor's pre-existing platform IP while granting the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free embedded-IP licence, (iii) adds the missing Customer Data ownership sentence, and (iv) bars joint ownership — matching the redline guidance without disturbing Licensor's legitimate platform ownership.

Edit is reasonably minimal: the existing Article III sentences are untouched and the override paragraph is sufficient to defeat the sweeping IP/Derivative Work definitions, so no separate rewrite of p0015 is needed. Deterministic checks confirm no residual assignment of Licensee data or IP to Licensor.

Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, prefixed, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position and expressly offers the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence) if assignment is refused.
